requirement:
The tracked source-read operation resolves the selected `OutlineData` through
the application's source-node mapping and reads that node through `Domain`.
Successful reads delivered to the caller record that node's identity and the
fingerprint of its supplied contents.

The graph's recording and freshness contracts apply under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
rationale:
The subject has three obligations. Its two cited graph requirements are context only.

1. **Mapping.** The read resolves the selected `OutlineData` through the application's source-node mapping.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns]` reads an unknown path and an unknown selector. Both return "unsupported source item", add no dependency, and cause no `Domain` read.
   - The same test shows a supported address reads the mapped node. `read_nodes` is `["source-node", "source-node"]`, so the mapped node identity is the one read.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions]` covers the model-tool path. It rejects an unknown node. It reads a listed node and returns the `Domain` text "a source snapshot", not the disk contents.

2. **Read through `Domain`.**
   - The direct test counts `Domain` reads and checks the returned contents, `"prepared contents"`.
   - It also makes the read fail with `fail_read`. The error is preserved and no dependency is recorded.

3. **Recording.** A successful delivered read records the node identity and the fingerprint of the supplied contents.
   - The direct test asserts the dependencies are exactly `Dependency::Node(source-node, returned.fingerprint())`, after the earlier failures. Only the successful return is recorded.
   - It then finishes a record and checks `is_current`. The record is current. After the `Domain` text changes it is not current. That ties the stored fingerprint to the actual contents.
   - The configured-agent test asserts exact `Dependency::Node` lists. The fingerprints are computed independently from the delivered source text, for both the opening node and the two read excerpts. Listings, rejected reads and repeated search finalization add nothing.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[cached_selected_source_reads_record_exact_delivered_contents_and_errors_add_no_input]` asserts the recorded fingerprint equals the exact selected content. Searches, outlines and a failed read of a missing selector add no input.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_tools_keep_search_discovery_separate_from_delivered_source_reads]` checks that a search does not record a dependency and a later read does.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` checks that listing, search, outline and paging record nothing.

The graph recording and freshness rules are cited context. They carry their own tests and need none here. No acknowledgments apply and I found no unmarked relevant tests. I found no gap.

The tracked source-read operation resolves the selected `OutlineData` through
the application's source-node mapping and reads that node through `Domain`.
Successful reads delivered to the caller record that node's identity and the
fingerprint of its supplied contents.
The graph's recording and freshness contracts apply under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
:::{req} node_inputs
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
:::{req} checking_records
The method is declared under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.check_inputs`.
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The method observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
